The Police Inspector of Sanjay Nagara Police Station submitted charge sheet against accused No.1 to 4 for the offences punishable under Section 120(B), 420, 468, 471, 204 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code.

2. Prosecution Case: Accused No.1 to 4 have constructed Shreya Apartment under the company in the name and style of Moksha Builders and Developers at New BEL Road, Jaladarshini Layout,
within the limits of Sanjay Nagara Police Station and in the said apartments, CW1 namely Smt.
Jayashree purchased Flat No. B-4 for a sum of Rs.38,00,000/- from obtaining loan from ABN Amro Bank and on 23- 01-2007 registered in the Sub-Register office of Peenya.

Thereafter, the accused No.1 assured CW1 that they will get loan for lesser rate of interest at ING Vysya Bank and transferred the documents from ABN Amro Bank to Vysya Bank and after that the accused No.1 to 4 have tried to purchase Flat at Shreya Apartment by pledging the documents of CW1 to ING Vysya Bank and obtained loan and thereafter made GPA to accused No.2 and on 18-03-2009 mentioned instead of B-4 No.24/9 Old flat No.TFB-4 and registered in the father name of accused No.1 in the office of Sub-Registrar, Hebbala and cheated the informant thereby committed the alleged offences.

prepared FIR as per Ex.P8 and sent the same to the Court and handed over the case papers to CW6.

In support of prosecution case as narrated in paragraph 2 and the point for consideration in paragraph 12 of this judgment, the prosecution examined the following witnesses i. CW1 by name Smt. Jayashree, being informant examined as PW1 deposed that, in the year 2006, the accused was running a real estate company called Moksha Builders and was building Shreya Apartment in Jaladarshini Layout on New BEL Road.
She purchased Plot No. B4 in the said apartment for KABC030771782018 CC No.28352/2018 about Rs. 36 lakhs and the accused sanctioned loan for Rs.32 lakhs from ABN Amro Bank.
She had been paying the loan installment every month.
In July 2008, the accused No.1 came and said that ING Vysya Bank had charging lesser rate of interest @ 10.5 %, so she should transfer the said loan to Vysya Bank.
She said that she would transfer her loan from ABN Amro Bank to ING Vysya Bank and obtained an additional loan therein and gave the same to accused No.1.

Since she was 8 months pregnant at that time, she signed all the documents for the loan transfer and for additional loan and gave the documents to the accused however ABN Amro Bank said that they would not give documents through anyone else.
The accused No.1 sent a GPA however she did not sign the same.
Then ABN Amro Bank told him to give the GPA in the form they provided for transfer of documents, so she gave the GPA to her brother namely Sri Harsha.
He said that he went to the said ABN Amro Bank and brought the relevant documents and gave them to the accused No 1.
Then he told him that loan had been sanctioned by ING Vysya Bank and that the said loan amount of Rs.47 lakhs had been deposited in the account of Moksha Builders.
Thereafter, he had been paying an installment of Rs.55,019/- every month to the said Vysya Bank since October 2008.
In the month of July 2009, the said bank called up and asked when will she get her house registered.
Then he went to the said bank and showed the documents regarding the registration of KABC030771782018 CC No.28352/2018 his house.
At that time, the accused had a new project in Nagashetty, which was situated at in C-3.

It is learnt that he had forged her signature in the Construction Agreement, Sale Agreement, Tri-partite Agreement, Loan Agreement and submitted the said documents to the bank to show that he had purchased the said C-3 plot and got the loan sanctioned.

Before proceedings with the Point No. 1, the discussion on forgery of document is significant in this case and hence the Point No. 2 has been taken up for consideration.

Section 468:- Forgery for purpose of cheating whoever commits forgery, intending that the document or electronic record forged shall be used for the purpose of cheating, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

1. Making a False Document 2.

KABC030771782018 CC No.28352/2018  Dishonestly or fraudulently making,

Dishonestly or fraudulently causing any person to sign, seal, execute, or alter a document or electronic record, knowing that the person does not know the contents or nature of the alteration due to unsoundness of mind or intoxication 5. Intention to Cause Damage, Injury, or Fraud 6.

The false document must be made with the intent to cause damage or injury to the public or KABC030771782018 CC No.28352/2018 any person, support any claim or title, cause a person to part with property, enter into a contract, or commit fraud.

on the date of registration of Ex.P7, the PW1 had knowledge about the sale deed dated 16/03/2009 however failed to challenge the same before the competent civil court or for lodging the criminal complaint.

So, the points No.2 for determination are decided against the prosecution and in favour of the defence.
21. Point No. 3: Whether the accused has used the forged GPA dated 07/01/2009 for purpose of cheating and used the same as the genuine document?

It is the case of prosecution that the accused No.1 to 4 has produced the forged GPA dated 07/01/2009 before Sub-registrar, Hebbal to cheat the Sub-registrar and PW1 for registering the sale deed dated 16/03/2009 as per Ex.P7.

When the prosecution failed to prove the forgery, the question of production of alleged GPA dated 07/01/2009 before Sub-registrar, Hebbal knowing fully well that the same is a fake document does not arise thereby the question of constituting the offence under section 471 of IPC was not made out.
It was further required to be proved that the GPA dated 07/01/2009 in question was forged and fabricated by the prosecution.
It was further required to be proved that the accused No.1 to 4 fraudulently and dishonestly used the GPA dated 07/01/2009 knowing or having reason to believe the same is forged and fabricated.

In the present case, the prosecution failed to prove that the GPA dated 07/01/2009 Jayashree vs B.M Girish on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71266568/
11 was forged and fabricated.
No evidence was led to the effect that the accused No.1 to 4 knew that GPA dated 07/01/2009 was forged and fabricated.

Under these circumstances, offence under Section 471 of IPC was also not proved against the accused thereby the point No.3 for determination is decided against the prosecution and in favour of the defence.
22. Point No. 1.
The prosecution claims that the accused committed offence under Section 420 of IPC.

According to Section 420 IPC, offence is made out against a person who cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person or to make alter or destroy the whole or part of any valuable security or anything which is signed or sealed, which is being capable of converted into valuable security.

In the instant case,
there is no allegation to the effect that the accused caused delivery of any property from PW1.

In so far as the question of forgery and fabrication of GPA dated 07/01/2009 is not proved, then the question of cheating does not arise and the said principle is appreciated in the case of Sheila Sebastian vs R.Jawaharaj and Ors reported in AIR 2018 SUPREME COURT 2434.

So, the point No.1 for determination is decided against the prosecution and in favour of the defence.

23. Point No.4: Whether the accused No.1 to 4 has criminally conspired together for commission of forgery and cheating?
Section 120A of IPC reads as under . Definition of criminal conspiracy.-- When two or more persons agree to do, or cause to be done, (1) an illegal act, or KABC030771782018 CC No.28352/2018 (2) an act which is not illegal by illegal means, such an agreement is designated a criminal conspiracy:
Provided that no agreement except an agreement to commit an offence shall amount to a criminal conspiracy unless some act besides the agreement is done by one or more parties to such agreement in pursuance thereof.
Explanation.
It is immaterial whether the illegal act is the ultimate object of such agreement, or is merely incidental to that object.]

[120B. Punishment of criminal conspiracy.--(1) Whoever is a party to a criminal conspiracy to commit an offence punishable with death, [imprisonment for life] or rigorous imprisonment for a term of two years or upwards, shall, where no express provision is made in this Code for the punishment of such a conspiracy, be punished in the same manner as if he had abetted such offence.

(2) Whoever is a party to a criminal conspiracy other than a criminal KABC030771782018 CC No.28352/2018 conspiracy to commit an offence punishable as aforesaid shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding six months, or with fine or with both.]

On perusal of the section 120A of IPC, the Prosecution has to prove that the accused No.1 to 4 have conspired together for cheating the CW1 however there is nothing on record to show either from the Jayashree vs B.M Girish on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71266568/
12 complaint, investigation case papers and from the evidence of PW1, how the accused No.1 , 3 and 4 were conspired with the accused 2 to prove the aforesaid charge under section 120B of IPC.

IO has not placed any substance to prove the criminal conspiracy of accused No.1, 3 and 4 with accused No.2 or to show that they had conspired together to commit the alleged offence thereby the Point No. 4 is answered in the negative.
24.

Therefore, in the light of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, the Court is of the considered opinion that the prosecution failed to prove the charges against the accused No.1 to 4 beyond all reasonable doubts consequently this accused is entitled for benefit of doubt.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
on the date of registration of Ex.P7, the PW1 had knowledge about the sale deed dated 16/03/2009 however failed to challenge the same before the competent civil court or for lodging the criminal complaint.
Under these circumstances, the prosecution has clearly failed to prove charge under Section 468 of IPC against the accused No.1 to 4.
It is the case of prosecution that the accused No.1 to 4 has produced the forged GPA dated 07/01/2009 before Sub-registrar, Hebbal to cheat the Sub-registrar and PW1 for registering the sale deed dated 16/03/2009 as per Ex.P7.
When the prosecution failed to prove the forgery, the question of production of alleged GPA dated 07/01/2009 before Sub-registrar, Hebbal knowing fully well that the same is a fake document does not arise thereby the question of constituting the offence under section 471 of IPC was not made out.
It was further required to be proved that the GPA dated 07/01/2009 in question was forged and fabricated by the prosecution.
It was further required to be proved that the accused No.1 to 4 fraudulently and dishonestly used the GPA dated 07/01/2009 knowing or having reason to believe the same is forged and fabricated.
In the present case, the prosecution failed to prove that the GPA dated 07/01/2009 Jayashree vs B.M Girish on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71266568/
11 was forged and fabricated.
No evidence was led to the effect that the accused No.1 to 4 knew that GPA dated 07/01/2009 was forged and fabricated.
Under these circumstances, offence under Section 471 of IPC was also not proved against the accused thereby the point No.3 for determination is decided against the prosecution and in favour of the defence.
The prosecution claims that the accused committed offence under Section 420 of IPC.
In the instant case,
there is no allegation to the effect that the accused caused delivery of any property from PW1.
In so far as the question of forgery and fabrication of GPA dated 07/01/2009 is not proved, then the question of cheating does not arise and the said principle is appreciated in the case of Sheila Sebastian vs R.Jawaharaj and Ors reported in AIR 2018 SUPREME COURT 2434.
Thus, no ingredient for offence under Section 420 IPC against the accused was made out.
On perusal of the section 120A of IPC, the Prosecution has to prove that the accused No.1 to 4 have conspired together for cheating the CW1 however there is nothing on record to show either from the Jayashree vs B.M Girish on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71266568/
12 complaint, investigation case papers and from the evidence of PW1, how the accused No.1 , 3 and 4 were conspired with the accused 2 to prove the aforesaid charge under section 120B of IPC.
IO has not placed any substance to prove the criminal conspiracy of accused No.1, 3 and 4 with accused No.2 or to show that they had conspired together to commit the alleged offence thereby the Point No. 4 is answered in the negative.

ORDER Acting U/Sec.248(1) of the Cr.P.C.
(i) The accused No.1 to 4 are found not guilty and acquitted from the offences punishable under Sec.120(B), 420, 468, 471 read with section 34 of Indian Penal Code.
(ii) Accused are set at liberty.
(iii) In view of Section 437-A of Cr.P.C their bail bonds shall be in force for 6 (six)
months.
